name: Emory Gordy Jr.
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 country-pop — Emory Gordy Jr.
notes: The bass-player-producer of the neotraditional wing, and the entry calls this "the strongest 'live-bass-as-melody' entry in this section." Two statements about the low end pull in different directions and both are encoded rather than one being dropped. The arrangement claim: "because the producer is the bassist, the rhythm section is written as a unit — model kick and bass as a single locked part rather than two independently-programmed ones," which is `rhythm: mirror_kick`. The content claim: "he plays bass on the records he produces, which makes the bass part the most compositional element in his productions — walking lines, chromatic approach notes, inversions under static chords, and a genuine countermelody role under the vocal," which is a low `followRootsProb` and the widest passing-tone set of any producer here. Locked onsets, free pitches — that is what a bassist-producer's line actually is, and the chord voicing is raised so the bass has room to reach up into it without overlapping. Drums are "a small, dry, roots-scaled kit; brushes and cross-stick are the default and the full backbeat is reserved for choruses." Harmony is "I–IV–V, I–♭VII–IV, and i–VII–VI on the minor cuts," with "mountain-modal and mixolydian colour on the Appalachian material." Vocal harmony is "mountain-style close intervals (parallel fourths and fifths as well as thirds)," which is the close voicing and the counter's octave/answer split. Form: "short songs, no post-chorus hooks, ensemble stop-endings." ⚠ Confidence is medium and the research says why: "career and instrument role documented; harmonic detail inferred from lane and roster [LOW-CONF]." ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are the velocity tiers, the perc density and the counter ratio.
